mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the past month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is negative, or if the correlation between GDP growth and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 2% in the past two months indicates a strong supply-side response, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signal a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment reacts to the potential economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and RSAFS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between HOUST and RSAFS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in the past month, coupled with a federal funds rate below 1%, indicates inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate further fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in the past month signals a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised upwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS shows positive growth, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
